tagline: Hands-free reading. The screen scrolls by itself.
serviceRequired: Turn on the accessibility service first
appsHint: Rolo only scrolls inside the apps you pick. Leave it empty to scroll everywhere.
tryPreview: Try it on a sample page
tip: Tip: hold the floating button to change the speed without leaving your book.
buttonHint: Tap to start or pause, hold to change speed, drag to move
disclosureWhy: Rolo uses the Android accessibility service to scroll for you. It is the only way an app can move the screen of another app, like your e-book or PDF reader.
disclosureDoes: What it does: simulates a slow upward swipe, at the speed you choose, only while scrolling is on.
disclosureDoesNot: What it does not do: it does not read, collect, store or share anything on your screen. Rolo has no internet access.
disclosureRestricted: If the switch is greyed out, open App info, tap ⋮ and choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
previewBody:
The lighthouse stood on the last rock before the open sea, and every evening Marta climbed its hundred and twelve steps to light the lamp.

She had counted them so many times that her feet knew the number before she did. The sixth step creaked, the fortieth was chipped, and on the ninety-first someone long ago had carved a small boat with a knife.

From the top she could see the whole bay: the fishing boats coming home, the gulls folding their wings on the harbour wall, the lights of the village going on one by one like slow fireflies.

That night the fog came early. It rolled over the water without a sound and swallowed the boats, the gulls and the village, until only the beam of the lighthouse was left, turning and turning in a world made of white.

Marta sat by the lamp with a cup of tea and a book she had read three times. Somewhere out there, a boat she could not see was steering by her light, and that was enough.
